answer: One-shot attestation edges: the first A-to-B attestation in an epoch counts at full weight, a second one on the same edge is worthless. Honest attest graphs are sparse, so nothing is lost. A sybil ring needs dense mutual webbing to look established; one-shot edges cap a ring's value at its distinct peers, and the only escape is minting fresh identities for fresh edge sets, so cost climbs linearly. The spiral of re-attestation dies at each vertex; the ring's haven is its density, and that is exactly what the rule burns.
